```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
if (!requireNamespace("forecast", quietly = TRUE)) stop("Install package 'forecast'.")
```

# 1. Settings

```{r settings}
workers         <- as.integer(Sys.getenv("STORE_SALES_WORKERS", "4"))  # cores used by final_forecast
lift_worker_cap <- TRUE                                    # see section 3
h               <- 16L
origins         <- as.Date(c("2017-07-14", "2017-07-30"))  # same windows as selection.Rmd
starts          <- as.Date(c("2013-01-01", "2015-01-01"))
cache_dir       <- "comparison_cache"                         # one file per run
dir.create(cache_dir, showWarnings = FALSE)
```

The model of `storesales.rmd` is fitted on data up to each window's cut-off,
from 2013 and from 2015, and forecasts the following 16 days. Each of the four
runs is saved, so an interrupted knit resumes where it stopped.

# 2. Data import

Same loading step as `storesales.rmd`, including the Good Friday correction.

```{r read-data}
data_dir <- Sys.getenv("STORE_SALES_DATA", "store-sales-time-series-forecasting")
if (!dir.exists(data_dir)) stop("Knit from the Kaggle folder containing the data directory.")
csv_files <- sort(list.files(data_dir, pattern = "\\.csv$", full.names = TRUE))
datasets <- setNames(lapply(csv_files, function(path) {
  x <- read.csv(path, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  if ("date" %in% names(x)) x$date <- as.Date(x$date)
  x
}), tools::file_path_sans_ext(basename(csv_files)))
required <- c("train", "test", "stores", "oil", "holidays_events",
              "transactions", "sample_submission")
stopifnot(all(required %in% names(datasets)))
train <- datasets$train; test <- datasets$test; stores <- datasets$stores
holidays_events <- datasets$holidays_events
# Data correction: Good Friday 2013 was March 29 (the file has April 29, a Monday)
holidays_events$date[holidays_events$description == "Viernes Santo" &
  holidays_events$date == as.Date("2013-04-29")] <- as.Date("2013-03-29")
```

# 3. Model functions

The function definitions are read directly from the `modeling-configuration`
chunk of `storesales.rmd`, so this file always uses the current version of
that model. Only the definitions are run; the chunk's checks, which require
training data to end on August 15, are skipped.

`final_forecast` limits itself to 8 workers. With `lift_worker_cap <- TRUE`,
that limit is removed in the copy loaded here (one expression,
`min(workers, 8L, n)` becomes `min(workers, n)`); `storesales.rmd` itself is
not changed and nothing else in the model is affected.

```{r load-model}
rmd <- readLines("storesales.rmd")
first <- grep("^```\\{r modeling-configuration", rmd)
last  <- first + grep("^```\\s*$", rmd[(first + 1L):length(rmd)])[1]
chunk <- rmd[(first + 1L):(last - 1L)]
if (lift_worker_cap) chunk <- sub("min(workers, 8L, n)", "min(workers, n)", chunk, fixed = TRUE)
is_function_definition <- function(e) is.call(e) && as.character(e[[1]]) %in% c("<-", "=") &&
  is.call(e[[3]]) && identical(e[[3]][[1]], as.name("function"))
for (e in parse(text = chunk)) if (is_function_definition(e)) eval(e, envir = globalenv())
stopifnot(exists("final_forecast"), exists("make_holiday_calendar"))

holiday_calendar <- make_holiday_calendar(stores, holidays_events,
  seq(as.Date("2013-01-01"), max(test$date), by = "day"))
```

For the 2015 runs, the training rows simply start in 2015. The model's
history always begins on 2013-01-01, so the earlier days enter as missing
sales, which its exact likelihood fits skip.

# 4. Runs

```{r runs}
run_storesales <- function(origin, start) {
  file <- file.path(cache_dir, paste0("storesales_", format(start, "%Y"), "_", format(origin), ".rds"))
  if (file.exists(file)) return(readRDS(file))
  tr <- train[train$date >= start & train$date <= origin, ]
  te <- train[train$date > origin & train$date <= origin + h,
              c("id", "date", "store_nbr", "family", "onpromotion", "sales")]
  fit <- final_forecast(tr, te[, c("id", "date", "store_nbr", "family", "onpromotion")],
                        holiday_calendar, workers = workers)
  out <- data.frame(window = format(origin), key = paste(te$store_nbr, te$family, sep = " | "),
                    family = te$family, date = te$date, actual = te$sales,
                    pred = fit$submission$sales[match(te$id, fit$submission$id)])
  saveRDS(out, file)
  out
}
storesales_runs <- list()
for (s in seq_along(starts)) {
  res <- do.call(rbind, lapply(origins, run_storesales, start = starts[s]))
  storesales_runs[[format(starts[s], "%Y")]] <- res
}
```

# 5. Comparison

All models are scored on the same rows: every series and day in both
windows, including series that never sold. The three models from
`selection.Rmd` are read from `selection_final.rds`.

```{r compare}
rmsle <- function(d) sqrt(mean((log1p(d$pred) - log1p(d$actual))^2))
ours <- readRDS("selection_final.rds")
models <- c(setNames(storesales_runs, paste0("storesales.rmd, from ", names(storesales_runs))),
  setNames(lapply(ours, `[[`, "results"),
           sapply(ours, function(f) paste0(f$structure, ", from ", format(f$start, "%Y")))))

row_id <- function(d) paste(d$window, d$key, d$date)
ref <- sort(row_id(models[[1]]))
stopifnot(all(vapply(models, function(d) identical(sort(row_id(d)), ref), TRUE)))

scores <- data.frame(model = names(models),
  pooled = vapply(models, rmsle, 0),
  w1 = vapply(models, function(d) rmsle(d[d$window == format(origins[1]), ]), 0),
  w2 = vapply(models, function(d) rmsle(d[d$window == format(origins[2]), ]), 0),
  row.names = NULL)
knitr::kable(scores[order(scores$pooled), ], digits = 4, row.names = FALSE,
  caption = "Holdout RMSLE (w1 = window to July 30, w2 = window to August 15)")

by_family <- sapply(models, function(d) sqrt(tapply((log1p(d$pred) - log1p(d$actual))^2, d$family, mean)))
knitr::kable(by_family[order(-by_family[, 1]), ], digits = 3, caption = "Pooled RMSLE by product family")

saveRDS(models, "comparison_results.rds")
```

# 6. Kaggle submission from 2015

The 2015 version did better on the holdout, so it is refitted on all
training data from 2015 to August 15 and forecasts the Kaggle test period.
`submission.csv` from `storesales.rmd` remains the 2013 version.

```{r submission}
sub_file <- "submission_storesales_2015.csv"
if (!file.exists(sub_file)) {
  fit <- final_forecast(train[train$date >= starts[2], ], test, holiday_calendar, workers = workers)
  write.csv(fit$submission, sub_file, row.names = FALSE)
}
```
